courses.description: Principles and applications of optical physics. Interference, diffraction, coherence, polarization, Fresnel relations, optical coatings, waves in dielectric media, Gaussian beams, waveguides, optical cavities, lasers, fibre optics, and Fourier optics. [3-3-0] Prerequisite: One of PHYS 301, PHYS 354 and one of MATH 215, MATH 255.

prereq.text: One of PHYS 301, PHYS 354 and one of MATH 215, MATH 255

courses.title: Experimental Physics
courses.description: A laboratory course with a wide choice of experiments for fourth year Honours and Major students. Topics include solid state, nuclear, classical, quantum, electromagnetic and low temperature physics. For six credits, two weekly laboratory periods and completion of a project in second term are required. [0-3-0] Prerequisite: One of PHYS 309, PHYS 319.

courses.title: Computational Physics
courses.description: Scientific programming applied to problems in physics. Fundamentals of numerical analysis for continuum problems. Solution of linear and non-linear algebraic systems, ordinary differential equations and stochastic problems. [3-0-1] Prerequisite: One of PHYS 312, MATH 257, MATH 316 and one of PHYS 210, EOSC 211, CPSC 110, CPSC 103, APSC 160.

prereq.text: One of PHYS 312, MATH 257, MATH 316 and one of PHYS 210, EOSC 211, CPSC 110, CPSC 103, APSC 160

courses.title: Quantum Physics
courses.description: Fundamentals of atomic, nuclear, particle, and condensed matter physics. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: MATH 215 and one of CHEM 312, PHYS 200.

prereq.text: MATH 215 and one of CHEM 312, PHYS 200

courses.title: Physics Demonstrations
courses.description: The students will prepare, under the supervision of a faculty member, a demonstration or series of demonstrations intended to illustrate physical principles to diverse audiences. Intended for third- or fourth-year Physics Majors and Math/Science Education students.

courses.title: Physics of Biocellular Structure and Machinery
courses.description: Molecular structure and architecture of biological cells, interactions of molecules in aqueous solution and at interfaces, physical properties of polymers and surfactants, mechanisms of cell membranes and cytoplasmic structures, thermodynamics of molecular machines and mechanical enzymes. Credit can not be given for both PHYS 437 and 537. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of PHYS 313, PHYS 403, PHYS 455, CHEM 304.

prereq.text: One of PHYS 313, PHYS 403, PHYS 455, CHEM 304

courses.title: Zoological Physics
courses.description: Animal systems viewed from a physicist's perspective. Topics include sensory systems, energy budgets, locomotion, internal flows, physical advantages of grouping. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157, SCIE 001. BIOL 325 is recommended. Equivalency: BIOL 438

prereq.text: One of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157, SCIE 001

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Physics
courses.description: Directed studies available to students in Honours Physics with approval from the Head of the Department.

courses.title: Honours Thesis
courses.description: A research project, undertaken under the direction of a faculty member, culminating in a thesis. [1*-6-0]

courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Postulates of quantum mechanics, expectation values, hermitian operators, commuting observables, applications to one-dimensional systems, harmonic oscillators, angular momentum, applications in three dimensions, hydrogen atom, time dependent perturbations. Credit will be granted for only one of PHYS 304, 450 or CHEM 312. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of PHYS 200, PHYS 250.

courses.title: Applied Electromagnetic Theory
courses.description: Wave propagation and related phenomena in dielectrics, conductors and plasmas. Wave guides, radiation, antennae, special relativity. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of PHYS 301, PHYS 354.

courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Introduction to quantum statistical mechanics and its application to systems of varying complexity from the simple ideal gas to the degenerate gas. Quantum fluids, phase transitions and simulation methods will also be introduced. Credit will be granted for only one of PHYS 403 or PHYS 455. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of PHYS 257, PHYS 203, PHYS 313 and one of PHYS 304, PHYS 450.

prereq.text: One of PHYS 257, PHYS 203, PHYS 313 and one of PHYS 304, PHYS 450

courses.title: Applied Optics
courses.description: Basic applications of lasers, geometrical optics, fibre optics, diffraction, and Fourier optics. [3-3-0] Prerequisite: All of PHYS 250, PHYS 354.

courses.title: Applied Nuclear Physics
courses.description: Radioactive decay and radiations, nuclear properties, interactions of neutrons, physical principles of power reactors, nuclear fusion, radiation monitoring, and safety. [3-0-1*] Prerequisite: One of PHYS 304, PHYS 450.

courses.title: Applied Solid State Physics
courses.description: Symmetry of crystal structures, reciprocal lattice, band theory, conduction in metals and semiconductors, phonons and superconductivity. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: One of PHYS 450, PHYS 304.

courses.title: Student Directed Seminar
courses.description: Self-directed, collaborative studies, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment, and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars. Cannot be used as a specialization requirement in any PHYS and/or ASTR specialization. [3-0-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
courses.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the fall term of the fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Physics. Prerequisite: PHYS 399. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Co-operative Work Placement V
courses.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer following the fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Physics. Prerequisite: PHYS 498. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Quantum Mechanics I
courses.description: Non-relativistic quantum mechanics with applications to atomic, nuclear and particle physics. Perturbation theory, multielectron atoms, molecular structure, WKB, scattering theory. Recommended pre-requisite: PHYS 402. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Quantum Mechanics II
courses.description: Time-dependent perturbation theory, density matrix formalism, NMR, emission and absorption of radiation. Elementary field theory techniques for many body systems. Quasiparticles, phonons, magnons, holes. Relativistic Klein-Gordon and Dirac equations. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics I
courses.description: One-electron theory of solids, energy bands, lattice vibration, transport theory. Prerequisite: A background in undergraduate solid state physics such as covered in PHYS 474 is highly recommended. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
courses.recommended: A background in undergraduate solid state physics such as covered in PHYS 474 is highly recommended

courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics II
courses.description: Interacting electrons, electron-phonon interaction, Hubbard model, magnetism, superconductivity, use of Green functions. Prerequisite: PHYS 502. Corequisite: PHYS 500. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

coreq.text: PHYS 500

courses.title: Special Relativity and Classical Electromagnetism
courses.description: Boundary-value problems, Green's functions and multipole expansions, magnetostatics, Faraday's law of induction, retarded potentials, Poynting's theorem and conservation laws, gauge invariance. Propagation of electromagnetic waves. Presentation of radiation from moving charges, classical electron theory. Prerequisite: A background in electricity and magnetism such as covered PHYS 401 is highly recommended. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
courses.recommended: A background in electricity and magnetism such as covered PHYS 401 is highly recommended

courses.title: Nuclear Physics
courses.description: Nucleons and their structure, hadrons and isospin, two-nucleon systems and interactions, bulk properties of nuclei and models, nuclear excitations and radioactivity, strong and electromagnetic decay, symmetries and weak interaction, reactions, nuclear astrophysics. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Quantum Field Theory II
courses.description: Prerequisite: PHYS 526. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Theory of Measurements
courses.description: Estimation of parameters from experimental measurements; maximum likelihood; least squares; tests of significance (chi square, etc). Noise properties of common devices. Extracting signals from noise; signal averaging; auto and cross-correlation, etc. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Modern Biophysics
courses.description: Fundamental concepts and advanced applications as used in current biophysics research. [3-0-0] This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Mean field theory, Landau theory of phase transitions, critical phenomena, renormalization theory. Monte Carlo method, linear response theory, fluctuations. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Superconductivity
courses.description: Conventional theories: BCS and Landau-Ginsburg, Josephson effect. New theories of high TC superconductivity. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Teaching Techniques in Physics and Astronomy
courses.description: Foundations of physics and astronomy education research, lesson plans, development of grading, effective questioning, effective presentations, methods in peer evaluation, and peer teaching. [1-0-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Group Theory Methods in Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Selected topics from atomic, molecular, solid state, nuclear and elementary particle physics treated by group theory methods. Prerequisite: PHYS 500. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Quantum Electronics and Nonlinear Optics
courses.description: Macroscopic and microscopic treatments of linear and non-linear response to electromagnetic fields. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Advanced Condensed Matter Physics
courses.description: Current issues in condensed matter theory. Prerequisite: All of PHYS 500, PHYS 503. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Laser Physics
courses.description: Classical and semi-classical treatment of interaction of EM-radiation with atomic systems; semi-classical laser theory; Gaussian beams and optical resonators; specific laser types and systems; femtosecond lasers and amplifiers; Raman lasers; lasing with inversion; topics of current research interest. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Radiotherapy Physics I
courses.description: Principles of dosimetry of ionizing radiation with emphasis on applications to radiotherapy and radiobiology. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.description: Clinical treatment planning techniques, quality assurance of treatment equipment and clinical decision making for radiation therapy. Quality assurance and decision making for medical imaging. Pass/fail. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Physics and Engineering of Particle Accelerators
courses.description: Injectors, radio frequency acceleration, superconducting acceleration elements, beam dynamics, and applications of electron accelerators. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Applications of Radioisotopes in Science and in Medicine
courses.description: Use of radioisotopes in nuclear medicine, materials science, environmental science, and nuclear physics in combination with the associated production, processing, and detection technologies. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
